name: Maiden Acoustic
reference: The acoustic guitar of 2 A.M. (The X Factor, 1995, Barnyard Studios, prod. Nigel Green and Steve Harris): dry, close and intimate under the verse
rig: One transcription (Karlsson's tab) marks the 2 A.M. intro and verse as acoustic, with a clean electric adding fills and distortion on the chorus; confirm by ear. The acoustic model, the player and any effects aren't documented, and a mic or DI is inferred. ToneMirror's 2 A.M. page is a JCM800 crunch setting for the electric only, so it doesn't apply here. Emulated as a double-tracked steel string from the electric alone: Diamond optical compressor, then two steel-string acoustic body IRs panned apart, then one small wooden room
notes: REBUILT (experiments D31). The old chain's 'piezo to Rode' NAM capture was the distortion the owner heard: THD -5 dB at guitar level, against -40 dB with it removed. This chain has no capture but the compressor: IRs are linear, so THD at -12 dBFS input is -41 dB at 110 Hz and -32 dB at 330 Hz. Left = Taylor 314 body IR, right = Collings D2H body IR, so the sides differ like two takes (Align wobble 0.15). The cab EQ (tone.csv) takes the magnetic pickup's low-mid hump down and opens the strings: -6 dB 100 Hz shelf, -5 dB 250, -2 dB 650, +2 dB 1.6 kHz, +10 dB 3.5 kHz, +10 dB 8 kHz shelf. Best on the neck pickup, picked lightly: nothing makes an electric fully acoustic. Room: Lexicon 480L Small Wood Room, 1.0 s, at the house reverb level.

left.label: Diamond Compressor, Comp 5 / EQ 6.5 / Vol 5 (levels the picking)
Lexicon 480L Small Wood Room 1.0 s (reverb only)

right.label: Collings D2H steel-string body IR (right acoustic)
Lexicon 480L Small Wood Room 1.0 s (reverb only)
